# Peramanathan Sathyamoorthy

> Senior Product and Systems Engineer · AI/SI agentic workflows, in Stockholm. 9+ years shipping web products, public APIs and CRM integrations in TypeScript, React, Next.js and Node.js (Oneflow, 2017–2024). Since December 2024: independent AI/SI product and systems engineering (agentic workflows). Maintains adaptate, a TypeScript library that validates streaming LLM tool-call JSON. It gets about 1,000 npm downloads a month per package (25 Oct–23 Nov 2026), and the latest release, 2.4.2, came out on 24 November 2026. EU work authorised, no sponsorship needed. Can start within two weeks of an offer.

This is the full profile. A short index is at https://captain.kingsparrow.space/llms.txt. Dated notes on ideas and working methods are at https://captain.kingsparrow.space/ideas.md. Oneflow work was closed-source.

## 1. Identity summary

Peramanathan Sathyamoorthy is a Senior Product and Systems Engineer in Stockholm, working on AI/SI agentic workflows, with over nine years of professional work on web products, public APIs, integrations and developer tooling, mostly in TypeScript, JavaScript, React and Node.js, with Python in production (Oneflow CRM integrations) and Rust in shipped open-source and desktop work. He holds an MSc in Computer Science from Uppsala University and an MSc in Operations Research and Computer Applications from NIT Tiruchirappalli, and he has two peer-reviewed papers on energy-efficient data communication for the mobile Internet of Things.

From April 2017 to December 2024 he worked at Oneflow AB in Stockholm, a digital signature and contract management platform. He started as a JavaScript Developer, built and led the Integration Team as a Full Stack Integration Engineer, led the engineering team as Engineering Team Lead, then moved to Senior Software Engineer for a TypeScript migration and permissions work. The precursor idea for a Zod-based validation library first appeared at Oneflow. adaptate, which he later shipped as public open source, was built from scratch; it is not a port of that internal library.

Since December 2024 his role has been Independent AI/SI product and systems engineering (agentic workflows). In that time he shipped:

- adaptate, a TypeScript validation library on npm (adaptate, @adaptate/core, @adaptate/utils). It turns one Zod or OpenAPI schema into per-screen views and validates streaming LLM tool-call JSON while it is still arriving. 2.4.2 was published from CI with SLSA provenance on 24 November 2026.
- kanithanj, a local-first decision app (Tauri, Rust, React, SQLite). Site: https://kanithanj-ai.vercel.app. Source: https://github.com/p10ns11y/collab-finder. 1.0.0 shipped on 19 August 2026 and 1.3.0 on 23 November 2026.
- Ensembly, a Rust service that gives several coding-agent tools one shared SQLite ledger and one approval flow.
- A marketplace of agent plugins and a skills library that install into Grok Build, Cursor and Claude Code.
- A Next.js portfolio and CV pipeline that renders the site, the PDF CV and these agent files from one data source.

Most of his deep-learning and systems work is private. The public repositories are a record that grew slowly.

## 5. Shipped work, in technical depth

### 5.1 adaptate: typed, validated data from any schema or stream

Links: https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate · https://adaptate-site.vercel.app · npm: adaptate, @adaptate/core, @adaptate/utils

adaptate is a TypeScript library built from scratch. From 25 October to 23 November 2026, npm downloads were @adaptate/core 1,092, @adaptate/utils 987 and adaptate 864 (counts include CI and bots), or about 1,000 a month per package. 2.4.2 of all three packages was published on 24 November 2026 from CI with SLSA provenance (predicate https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1). First commit 2 November 2024 (f506830); first npm publish of adaptate on 4 November 2024.

The problem. One data model is used by many screens and services, but each one needs different fields to be present. Copies of the schema drift. A model also streams a tool call as JSON, and `JSON.parse` throws until the last byte arrives, so the UI shows nothing.

Design.

- One schema, many views. `transformSchema(schema, config)` in @adaptate/core takes one Zod schema and a config for which fields a consumer needs, and returns a Zod schema with the same inferred type.
- OpenAPI interop both ways in @adaptate/utils, including `$ref` resolution.
- Streaming validation of LLM tool-call JSON as it arrives (`createAgUiPartialValidator`, `createStreamValidator`, `parseStream`), including a Result API so an AI/SI model's tool call can be checked at the boundary.

Numbers. On a 966-character sample, the incremental feed made 966 character visits; re-parsing the growing buffer made 68,304. Tests run converters on documents 100,000 levels deep. A `$ref` chain past depth 500 throws `RangeError`. CI fails a pull request if a timed case is more than 5% slower than its base, and packed tarballs are checked on TypeScript 7 and 6.

### 5.2 kanithanj: a local-first decision app (Tauri, Rust, React, SQLite)

Site: https://kanithanj-ai.vercel.app · source: https://github.com/p10ns11y/collab-finder · walkthrough: https://captain.kingsparrow.space/shipped/collab-finder

Releases v1.0.0 (19 August 2026) to v1.3.0 (23 November 2026), about 300 commits. A Rust backend with a SQLite ledger, LLM routing across providers, the xAI API, and secrets in the OS keyring. The model is called only when cost, fit and rate checks pass. A person approves before anything leaves the machine. Personal data never leaves disk. CI runs `cargo test` and Stryker mutation testing.

### 5.3 Ensembly: one shared ledger and one approval flow

Link: https://github.com/thecuriousts/ensembly · essays: https://captain.kingsparrow.space/articles

A Rust service, rebuilt from 13 July 2026 (tag v0.2.0), that gives several coding-agent tools one shared SQLite ledger and one approval flow. Bots and harnesses propose; Ensembly authorises, claims and completes. One writer owns the ledger, with idempotent retries (PR #91).

### 5.4 Agent plugins marketplace

Link: https://github.com/p10ns11y/plugins (first commit 15 July 2026). One repository of plugins that install into Grok Build, Claude Code and Cursor, bundling skills, commands, agents and hooks, including pulse-memory, live-engine, and routing and planning plugins.

### 5.5 Agent skills library

Link: https://github.com/p10ns11y/skills (first commit 8 June 2026). A library of `SKILL.md` procedures for context, coordination, supply-chain hardening, reviewable PRs and related work. In the README's words: "Most agent failures are not model failures. They are context, coordination, and guardrail failures."

### 5.6 devprofile: portfolio, CV pipeline and agent profile

Links: https://captain.kingsparrow.space · https://github.com/p10ns11y/devprofile (first commit 8 September 2025). Next.js 16, React 19 and TypeScript. One `cvdata.json` file drives the site, the PDF CV and the agent profile files, so content cannot drift. The site serves `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` as plain text.

### 5.7 imm: independent module maintainer

Link: https://github.com/p10ns11y/imm (first commit 22 September 2026, Rust). A supply-chain tool that installs a direct dependency as source and keeps other uses as hashed, audited extracts. An agent cannot approve its own extract.

### 5.8 proposales-planner-bench

Links: https://proposales-planner-bench.vercel.app · https://github.com/p10ns11y/proposales-planner-bench (first commit 6 October 2026). A public Next.js bench against the Proposales API, used to validate API readers with adaptate and to try planner-style workflows. Named after that API; it is a benchmark, not a product for that company.

### 5.9 thepulimaangani: Tamil prosody in the browser

Links: https://github.com/p10ns11y/thepulimaangani · walkthrough: https://captain.kingsparrow.space/shipped/thepulimaangani. A Rust parser for Tamil metre, compiled to WebAssembly, with a React UI. The analysis runs in the browser with no backend.

## 6. How I work

- Measure before trusting: retrieval benchmarks before ranking changes; performance budgets that fail a PR more than 5% slower.
- Rules enforced by tooling: README examples run as tests; 2.4.2 published from CI with provenance; hooks that ask before `git push` and deny force-push.
- Verify before irreversible acts: merges, releases, payments, deletions.
- Small, reviewable PRs; one source of truth for data.
- The same idea since his MSc research (IEEE CloudCom 2015): cut the cost of each observation while decisions improve. Today that means agents load only the context that can change the next step. Essays: https://captain.kingsparrow.space/articles
- Dated notes and earlier working methods: https://captain.kingsparrow.space/ideas.md
